reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 15.2(a)(i) lets Sanofi (our side) assign to any Affiliate without RevMed's consent, and 15.2(a)(ii) permits assignment of the whole Agreement to a successor in a sale of substantially all relevant assets or a merger/acquisition — exactly the preferred M&A/affiliate carve-out, confirmed by the deterministic check.

No asymmetry against us and no Vendor exit on our change of control: RevMed's Affiliate assignments are consent-gated (not unreasonably withheld), its Licensed Patent transfers to Third Parties require our consent (15.2(b)), Acquiror-side assignments are fenced by the firewall conditions (A)-(D), and no cited provision gives RevMed a termination or re-pricing right triggered by a Sanofi change of control.

Even on the least favourable reading (RevMed's successor assignment on its own CoC is not consent-gated and there is no express bar on assignment to a Sanofi competitor), the clause sits at or above the fallback (mutual successor assignment; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld), so these are correctly noted as sub-elements rather than redlined — flagging them would be over-flagging.

Correctly defers the Section 12.3 royalty cut-off on a Sanofi Change of Control to the termination-effects rule rather than double-flagging it here; it is a back-end economic consequence, not a Vendor exit or re-price right under ASSIGN.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline text was changed and no counterparty comment was produced, so the output is retained internal evidence only and no actionable proposal is required.
